subject: Telemetry sample, redaction notes, and access steps for FinServ compliance review
messages:
From: Glen Cooper <glen.cooper@finserv.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finserv.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: telemetry samples and redact guidance for compliance review

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team needs a small set of telemetry and log extracts demonstrating Redwood's misuse monitoring and alerting pipeline so we can validate retention, redaction, and event schemas. Specifically they asked for:

- A 24-hour sample of detection events (sampled) with metadata fields (event_type, model_id, routing_policy, sample_prefix, alert_severity)
- Examples of the alert message that would be delivered to an SIEM/PagerDuty integration
- The logging schema / column definitions for the retention matrix
- Notes on how customer PII is redacted or tokenized before leaving the private deployment

We can accept redacted samples; please indicate what was redacted and why. We also need any access controls you require if we ask for larger exports later (S3 presigned link, signed NDA, least-privilege IAM role, etc.).

Can you turn around something by EOD Tuesday so we can slot it into our 4/21 review?

—Glen
Senior Security Engineer
FinServ Bank

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Glen Cooper <glen.cooper@finserv.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finserv.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: telemetry samples and redact guidance for compliance review

Glen —

We can provide a redacted 24-hour sample and the logging matrix. High level summary up front: we run deterministic token hashing for any PII keys referenced in logs, redact free-text user content in exports unless explicitly requested under a DPA/NDA, and truncate numerical identifiers to preserve utility while avoiding full exposure. Attached README will document the exact regexes and hashing format used for each field.

Karthik — looping you in to confirm if we should include both the internal alert envelope and the SIEM-forwarded normalized example in the same bundle, or deliver SIEM examples in a follow-up. Marissa, can you prepare the zipped sample (telemetry + schema) and a short notes file describing what fields were redacted and the reasoning? Use the FinServ NDA template if they ask for a larger bundle.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: telemetry samples and redact guidance for compliance review

Jordan / Marissa —

Include two SIEM variants: (1) the raw internal alert envelope we use for ops (JSON) and (2) the normalized event we send to customer SIEMs (fields redacted/truncated). Redaction rules for the sample: replace any matching email, SSN, or card-number patterns with a token like <REDACTED_EMAIL_HASH:sha256> or <REDACTED_DIGITS:xxxx>. For large-volume detectors sample ~2% of events; for low-volume/high-severity detectors include all events in the window. Add a top-of-file audit header with sampling_rate, redaction_map, and generator_version.

Marissa — please produce: 1) safety_telemetry_sample.jsonl (redacted, with header), 2) logging_matrix.csv (field definitions + retention tiers), 3) access_readme.txt (presigned S3 link instructions, validity window, IAM role requirements). I will review the README before sharing externally.

—Karthik
Head of Applied ML — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Glen Cooper <glen.cooper@finserv.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finserv.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: telemetry samples and redact guidance for compliance review

Glen / Priya —

Attached (zipped) is the small bundle for the 24-hour window you requested: 

- safety_telemetry_sample.jsonl (2,400 events; header documents sampling_rate=0.02, redaction_map; emails and phones replaced with sha256 token stubs; free-text payloads omitted)
- logging_matrix.csv (field, type, retention_days, example_value)
- access_readme.txt (S3 presigned link, 48-hour validity, minimal IAM permissions required for expanded exports, and contact for audited export requests)

Attachment stubs: [safety_telemetry_sample.jsonl (application/jsonl)], [logging_matrix.csv (text/csv)], [access_readme.txt (text/plain)].

Notes on redaction: emails -> <REDACTED_EMAIL_HASH:sha256>, phone -> <REDACTED_PHONE_HASH:sha256>, numeric IDs -> last4 preserved, model payloads containing user-submitted content were excluded from this sample and require a DPA/NDA + additional access controls to export.

If you'd like, we can generate a single SIEM-forwarded CEF/JSON example mapped to your schema by EOD Wednesday; please share required mapping fields (e.g., eventCategory, severity, srcUser).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: safety_telemetry_sample.jsonl, logging_matrix.csv, access_readme.txt
